theme: ज्ञान का निखार: पृथ्वी, अग्नि, जीवन और तप में भगवान की उपस्थिति / Wisdom in the world: fragrance, radiance, life, and austerity as divine presence.
context: Krishna has already taught that all creation is grounded in Him and that He is both the supreme reality and the sustaining source of the cosmos. In this verse He gives concrete examples of how divine presence is not abstract alone but can be recognized in the order and vitality of the world.
contextHindi: श्रीकृष्ण पहले ही बता चुके हैं कि सब कुछ उनके भीतर है और वे सबका आधार हैं। अब वे यह दिखा रहे हैं कि पृथ्वी की मधुर गंध, अग्नि की ज्योति, जीवन की ऊर्जा और तप की दृढ़ता—ये सब भगवान की ही अभिव्यक्तियाँ हैं, जिससे अर्जुन को जगत को दिव्य दृष्टि से देखने की शिक्षा मिलती है।
sanskritDevanagari:
पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ |
जीवनं सर्वभूतेषु तपश्चास्मि तपस्विषु ||७-९||
transliteration:
puṇyo gandhaḥ pṛthivyāṃ ca tejaścāsmi vibhāvasau .
jīvanaṃ sarvabhūteṣu tapaścāsmi tapasviṣu ||7-9||

wordByWord.meaning: puṇya-gandhaḥ: the pure, wholesome fragrance; the sweet, life-giving quality that makes earth pleasant and sustaining.
pṛthivyām: in the earth; the material world as the ground of nourishment and beauty.
tejaḥ: radiance, brilliance, fire-energy; the illuminating power that transforms and purifies.
jīvanam: life-force, vitality; the animating principle present in all living beings.
tapaḥ: austerity, disciplined effort, inner heat and self-restraint; not mere discomfort but conscious refinement.
tapasviṣu: among ascetics; those who cultivate inward discipline and self-mastery.

spokenHindi: TEXT: श्रीकृष्ण कहते हैं, ‘पृथ्वी की मधुर गंध, अग्नि की ज्योति, सभी प्राणियों का जीवन, और तपस्वियों का तप—मैं ही हूँ।’ यह श्लोक केवल सुंदर शब्दों की कविता नहीं है; यह बताता है कि जगत की शुभता, उजाला, जीवन-शक्ति और अनुशासन—ये सब भगवान की उपस्थिति के रूप हैं। हम अक्सर संसार को भौतिक या अलग मानते हैं, लेकिन यहाँ कृष्ण कह रहे हैं कि जीवन के कई स्तरों में जो सुंदर, शुद्ध और शक्तिशाली है, वह उसी एक आधार से आता है। INFERENCE: इसका अर्थ यह नहीं है कि हर चीज़ में भगवान का मूल्य समान रूप से दिखाई देता है, बल्कि यह है कि जीवन के सर्वोत्तम रूपों में भी वही तत्त्व काम कर रहा है—जो शुद्धता, विवेक और शक्ति को संभव बनाता है।
clearEnglish: TEXT: Krishna declares that He is the sweet fragrance in the earth, the brilliance in fire, the life in all beings, and the austerity of ascetics. This is not simply poetic language. It says that the wholesome, energizing, and ordered dimensions of life arise from the same divine source that underlies the cosmos. The verse calls attention to qualities that make existence feel alive, coherent, and meaningful. INFERENCE: The point is not that every object is equally divine in a simplistic sense, but that the deepest source of life, discernment, and disciplined effort is one divine reality. When we see purity, radiance, vitality, or seriousness in life, we can recognize a sacred order beneath appearances rather than treating them as mere accident or materiality.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse plainly names four divine expressions: fragrance in earth, light in fire, life in beings, and austerity in ascetics. It emphasizes a sacred presence within ordinary life-processes rather than only in transcendence.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: From this, we can infer that the divine is not confined to temples or metaphysical abstractions; it can be recognized in nourishment, energy, consciousness, and disciplined effort. The inference is about source and meaning, not a claim that all forms are morally equal.

practicalApplication.label: Noticing the sacred
practicalApplication.text: When you eat food, sit in sunlight, or notice a calm moment of focus, pause and recognize that nourishment, clarity, and vitality are not merely material—they are also expressions of a larger order.

practicalApplication.label: Austerity with balance
practicalApplication.text: Practice disciplined habits—sleep, speech, attention, and effort—without turning them into self-hatred. The verse links tapas with the divine, not with harshness alone.

reflectionQuestion: In what parts of ordinary life do you most clearly feel a sense of sacred order, and how does that change your attention?
reflectionQuestionHindi: आपके लिए रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी में कौन-से हिस्से सबसे ज़्यादा दिव्य क्रम महसूस करते हैं, और यह आपकी निगाह को कैसे बदलते हैं?
